To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intermodal Ramin overlap coefficients of a few-mode optical fiber are strongly dependent on the pump power and on the mode content of both pump and signal, and that the mode-equalized distributed Raman gain in such a fiber is only slightly dependent on the mode content.
we experimentally characterize all intermodal overlap integrals for a few-mode fiber and demonstrate a mode differential gain of 0.25 dB for a two-mode signal.

the intermodal Rama intensity overlaps of a two-mode fiber can be characterized using Raman amplification and that the differential gain between the two mode-groups of the signal can be reduced to less than 0.25 dB for 10 dB overall gain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the Raman intensity overlaps and their impact on the amplification of mode-division multiplexed signals.
the experimental characterization of Raman intensity overlaps in a few-mode fiber.
the characterization of Raman overlap factors in few-mode optical fibers and their impact on mode-division multiplexed signal amplification.

The main takeaway from our work is that
Raman amplification in multi-mode fibers is feasible with low differential gain and can be used for distributed mode-equalized amplification.
the intermodal Ramin intensity overlaps of the few-mode fiber are not only a function of the mode-group, but also a function of the input pump power.
the Raman intensity overlap between mode groups is a critical factor in Raman amplification, which has to be taken into consideration for mode-division multiplexed systems.
